faq: Which robot do I need?

It depends on the task, the environment and the volume. Large-surface cleaning is a job for the RHC5, the MT1 or the MT1 Max; customer service is handled by the RHA3 and RHX2 families; industrial manipulation, by the RHG2; internal material transport, by the T150, T300, T600 and MP2000 AMRs; and outdoor or rough-terrain inspection, by the D5W quadruped. We help you choose with prior advice.
Do I need to program the robot?

Not for standard use: the models come with a ready-made skill set that runs multiple functions from day one. If you want to develop your own applications, open versions are available (RHX2 Ultra and RHX2 EDU) with an SDK, simulators and documented interfaces.
Can it be adapted to my company?

Yes. We start with prior advice to understand your use case, and we configure the robot, its routines and its behaviour to match your operations. This includes installation, commissioning and training for your team.
What maintenance do they require?
Regular preventive maintenance of joints, batteries and sensors, plus software updates. We offer an ongoing maintenance and support service to keep the equipment available.
Can it be rented instead of bought?
Get in touch with us. Depending on the model and the length of the project, we can offer purchase or rental, including commissioning and support.

posts.titulo: How to prepare your company for humanoid robotics
posts.resumen: Key points for evaluating processes, spaces and objectives before investing.
posts.cuerpo:
Bringing in a humanoid robot doesn't start with the robot, but with the process you want to solve. Before asking for a quote, it helps to be clear about which task needs covering, how many hours a day, and what result you expect.

Define the task, not the model

The same space might need a cleaning robot, a customer-service robot, or neither. Describe the task with numbers: floor area, time slots, the volume of people or parts, and what happens today when staff are short.

Review the environment

Corridor width, ramps, lifts, automatic doors, wifi coverage and charging points determine which models fit. A prior site visit avoids surprises during commissioning.

Think about who will use it

The team that works alongside the robot needs training and a clear day-to-day procedure: start-up, incidents, cleaning and basic maintenance.

Calculate the return with your own data

Compare the cost of the robot and its maintenance with the hours it frees up and the current cost of the task. A well-sized project stands on numbers, not expectations.

posts.resumen: Retail, industry, education and events are already adopting this technology.
posts.cuerpo:
Humanoid and service robotics are already at work in real environments. These are the uses that companies ask us about most.

Retail and customer service

Visitor reception, basic information, in-store guidance and brand activations. The robot doesn't replace the team: it absorbs repetitive questions and frees up time for sales.

Industry and logistics

Moving light material between workstations, facility inspection and support for repetitive line tasks. Here, autonomy, payload and integration with existing systems matter most.

Professional cleaning

Large indoor surfaces with fixed routes: supermarkets, stations, industrial units and shopping centres. This is the most mature use case, and the one that pays for itself soonest.

Education and research

Universities and training centres use open platforms to develop and test their own applications, with SDKs and simulators.

posts.titulo: Five questions before adding a cleaning robot
posts.resumen: Surface area, flooring, water, daily routine and support: what's worth measuring before deciding.
posts.cuerpo:
An autonomous cleaning robot performs well when the space and the operation support it. Before deciding, it's worth answering these five questions.

1. How many square metres need cleaning, and in how much time?

Performance is measured in square metres per hour under real conditions, including turns, obstacles and charging stops.

2. What is the floor like?

A continuous floor is not the same as one with joints, grilles or level changes. The type of floor determines the scrubbing system and water consumption.

3. Where does it fill and empty?

You need an accessible water point and drain, close to the work area and the charging point.

4. Who starts it up each day?

It's worth assigning a person responsible and a short start-up and check routine. Most incidents are avoided with two minutes of inspection.

5. What happens if it breaks down?

Ask about the support response time, spare-parts stock and exactly what the maintenance covers.

faq: Who is Bonico?
Bonico is our RHX2 Ultra: 1.31 m tall, 3D perception and 30 degrees of freedom. You can see its full technical sheet in the catalogue.
How much does it cost to hire Bonico?
The service is available from 1,200 € + VAT per day. The final price depends on the duration, the location and the customisation required.
Can Bonico dance?
Yes. Bonico can perform different dances and choreographies. We can also look into bespoke choreographies.
Can it talk to visitors?
Yes. Bonico can interact with visitors and hold conversations depending on the capabilities and set-up you book.
Can we customise its personality?
Yes. We can adapt certain aspects of Bonico's personality, dialogue, behaviour and content to your brand or your event.
Does the price include travel?
We travel to events anywhere in the world. Travel, accommodation and subsistence are quoted separately depending on the location and the duration of the event.
Is there an operator during the event?
Yes. The service includes supervision and technical assistance throughout the event.
Can we hire it for several days?
Yes. For trade fairs and multi-day events we can put together a specific proposal.
